functions.name: add_local_rport
functions.doc: Add **rport** parameter to local generated Via header -- see RFC3581. In effect for forwarded SIP requests.

functions.name: break
functions.doc: 'break' statement can be used to end a 'case' block in a 'switch' statement or exit from a 'while' statement.

functions.name: drop
functions.doc: Stop the execution of the configuration script and alter the implicit action which is done afterwards.

functions.name: exit
functions.doc: Stop the execution of the configuration script -- it has the same behaviour as return(0). It does not affect the implicit action to be taken after script execution.

functions.name: error
functions.doc: Not properly implemented yet - prints a log messages with the two string parameters.

functions.name: exec
functions.doc: Basic implementation of executing an external application with C `system()` function. Look also at the functions exported by `exec` module.

functions.name: force_rport
functions.doc: The `force_rport()` adds the rport parameter to the first Via header of the received message. Thus, Kamailio will add the received port to the top most Via header in the SIP message, even if the client does not indicate support for rport. This enables subsequent SIP messages to return to the proper port later on in a SIP transaction.

functions.name: add_rport
functions.doc: Alias for force_rport();

functions.name: force_send_socket
functions.doc: Force to send the message from the specified socket (it **must** be one of the sockets specified with the `listen` directive). If the protocol doesn't match (e.g. UDP message "forced" to a TCP socket) the closest socket of the same protocol is used.

functions.name: force_tcp_alias
functions.doc: **Alias name:** **add_tcp_alias**

functions.name: forward
functions.doc: Forward in stateless mode the SIP request to destination address set in `$du` or `$ru`.

functions.name: isflagset
functions.doc: Test if a flag is set for current processed message (if the flag value is 1). The value of the parameter can be in range of 0..31.

functions.name: is_int
functions.doc: Checks if a pseudo variable argument contains integer value.

functions.name: log
functions.doc: Write text message to standard error terminal or syslog. You can specify the log level (the integer id) as first parameter.

functions.name: prefix
functions.doc: Add the string parameter in front of username in R-URI.

functions.name: return
functions.doc: The return() function allows you to return any integer value from a called route() block. You can test the value returned by a route using `$retcode` variable (which is same as `$rc` or `$?`).

functions.name: return_mode
functions.doc: Control the return code evaluation mode:

functions.name: revert_uri
functions.doc: Set the R-URI to the value of the R-URI as it was when the request was received by server (undo all changes of R-URI).

functions.name: rewritehostport
functions.doc: **Alias name:** **sethostport, sethp**

functions.name: rewritehostporttrans
functions.doc: **Alias name:** **sethostporttrans, sethpt**

functions.name: rewritehost
functions.doc: **Alias name:** **sethost, seth**

functions.name: rewriteport
functions.doc: **Alias name:** **setport, setp**

functions.name: rewriteuri
functions.doc: **Alias name:** **seturi**

functions.name: rewriteuserpass
functions.doc: **Alias name:** **setuserpass, setup**

functions.name: rewriteuser
functions.doc: **Alias name:** **setuser, setu**

functions.name: route
functions.doc: Execute route block given in parameter. Parameter may be name of the block or a string valued expression.

functions.name: selval
functions.doc: Select a value based on conditional expression.

functions.name: set_advertised_address
functions.doc: Same as `advertised_address` but it affects only the current message. It has priority if `advertised_address` is also set.

functions.name: set_advertised_port
functions.doc: Same as `advertised_port` but it affects only the current message. It has priority over `advertised_port`.

functions.name: set_forward_no_connect
functions.doc: The message will be forwarded only if there is already an existing connection to the destination. It applies only to connection oriented protocols like TCP and TLS (TODO: SCTP), for UDP it will be ignored. The behavior depends in which route block the function is called:

functions.name: set_forward_close
functions.doc: Try to close the connection (the one on which the message is sent out) after forwarding the current message. Can be used in same route blocks as `set_forward_no_connect()`.

functions.name: set_reply_no_connect
functions.doc: Like `set_forward_no_connect()`, but for replies to the current message (local generated replies and replies forwarded by tm). The behavior depends in which route block the function is called:

functions.name: set_reply_close
functions.doc: Like `set_reply_no_connect`, but closes the TCP connection after sending. Can be used in same route blocks as `set_reply_no_connect`.

functions.name: setflag
functions.doc: Set a flag for current processed message. The value of the parameter can be in range of 0..31. The flags are used to mark the message for special processing (e.g., accounting) or to keep some state (e.g., message authenticated).

functions.name: strip
functions.doc: Strip the first N-th characters from username of R-URI (N is the value of the parameter).

functions.name: strip_tail
functions.doc: Strip the last N-th characters from username of R-URI (N is the value of the parameter).

functions.name: udp_mtu_try_proto
functions.doc: - proto - `TCP|TLS|SCTP|UDP` - like `udp_mtu_try_proto` global parameter but works on a per packet basis and not globally.

functions.name: userphone
functions.doc: Add `user=phone` parameter to R-URI.

params.name: advertised_address
params.doc: It can be an IP address or string and represents the address advertised in Via header. If empty or not set (default value) the socket address from where the request will be sent is used.

params.name: advertised_port
params.doc: The port advertised in Via header. If empty or not set (default value) the port from where the message will be sent is used. Same warnings as for 'advertised_address'.

params.name: alias
params.doc: **Alias name:** **domain**

params.name: async_workers
params.doc: Specify how many child processes (workers) to create for asynchronous execution in the group "default". These are processes that can receive tasks from various components (e.g, modules such as async, acc, sqlops) and execute them locally, which is different process than the task sender.

params.name: async_nonblock
params.doc: Set the non-block mode for the internal sockets used by default group of async workers.

params.name: async_usleep
params.doc: Set the number of microseconds to sleep before trying to receive next task (can be useful when async_nonblock=1).

params.name: async_workers_group
params.doc: Define groups of asynchronous worker processes.

params.name: async_tkv_evcb
params.doc: Set the name of the event route or KEMI callback for processing tkv.

params.name: async_tkv_gname
params.doc: Set the name of the async group to be used for processing TKV events. The async group has to be defined.

params.name: auto_aliases
params.doc: **Alias name:** **auto_domains**

params.name: auto_bind_ipv6
params.doc: When turned on, Kamailio will automatically bind to all IPv6 addresses (much like the default behaviour for IPv4).

params.name: bind_ipv6_link_local
params.doc: If set to `1`, try to bind also IPv6 link local addresses by discovering the scope of the interface. If set to `2`, skip binding link local addresses.

params.name: check_via
params.doc: Check if the address in top most via of replies is local. Default value is 0 (check disabled).

params.name: children
params.doc: Number of children to fork for the UDP interfaces (one set for each interface - ip:port). Default value is 8. For example if you configure the proxy to listen on 3 UDP ports, it will create 3xchildren processes which handle the incoming UDP messages.

params.name: chroot
params.doc: The value must be a valid path in the system. If set, Kamailio will chroot (change root directory) to its value.

params.name: corelog
params.doc: Set the debug level used to print some log messages from core, which might become annoying and don't represent critical errors. For example, such case is failure to parse incoming traffic from the network as SIP message, due to someone sending invalid content.

params.name: coreparam
params.doc: This parameter offers a generic framework to set new core parameters without the need to write new code in Lex/Yacc, but to add to an internal exports structure in the core. The format is:

params.name: debug
params.doc: Set the debug level. Higher values make Kamailio to print more debug messages. Log messages are usually sent to syslog, except if logging to stderr was activated (see [#log_stderror](#log_stderror) parameter).

params.name: description
params.doc: **Alias name:** **descr desc**

params.name: disable_core_dump
params.doc: Can be 'yes' or 'no'. By default core dump limits are set to unlimited or a high enough value. Set this config variable to 'yes' to disable core dump-ing (will set core limits to 0).

params.name: disable_tls
params.doc: **Alias name:** **tls_disable**

params.name: enable_tls
params.doc: **Alias name:** **tls_enable**

params.name: tls_connection_match_domain
params.doc: Value: `yes`/`no` (default `no`)

params.name: exit_timeout
params.doc: **Alias name:** **ser_kill_timeout**

params.name: flags
params.doc: SIP message (transaction) flags can have string names. The *name* for flags cannot be used for **branch** or **script flags**(\*)

params.name: force_rport
params.doc: Value: `yes`/`no` (default `no`)

params.name: fork
params.doc: If set to 'yes' the proxy will fork and run in daemon mode - one process will be created for each network interface the proxy listens to and for each protocol (TCP/UDP), multiplied with the value of 'children' parameter.

params.name: fork_delay
params.doc: Number of usecs to wait before forking a process.

params.name: group
params.doc: **Alias name:** **gid**

params.name: http_reply_parse
params.doc: Alias: http_reply_hack

params.name: ip_free_bind
params.doc: Alias: ipfreebind, ip_nonlocal_bind

params.name: ipv6_hex_style
params.doc: Can be set to `a`, `A` or `c` to specify if locally computed string representation of IPv6 addresses should be expanded lowercase, expanded uppercase or compacted lowercase hexa digits.

params.name: kemi.onsend_route_callback
params.doc: Set the name of callback function in the KEMI script to be executed as the equivalent of `onsend_route` block (from the native configuration file).

params.name: kemi.received_route_callback
params.doc: Set the name of callback function in the KEMI script to be executed as the equivalent of `event_route[core:msg-received]` block (from the native configuration file). For execution, it also require to have the received_route_mode global parameter set to 1.

params.name: kemi.reply_route_callback
params.doc: Set the name of callback function in the KEMI script to be executed as the equivalent of `reply_route` block (from the native configuration file).

params.name: kemi.pre_routing_callback
params.doc: Set the name of callback function in the KEMI script to be executed as the equivalent of `event_route[core:pre-routing]` block (from the native configuration file).

params.name: latency_cfg_log
params.doc: If set to a log level less or equal than debug parameter, a log message with the duration in microseconds of executing request route or reply route is printed to syslog.

params.name: latency_limit_action
params.doc: Limit of latency in us (micro-seconds) for config actions. If a config action executed by cfg interpreter takes longer than its value, a message is printed in the logs, showing config path, line and action name when it is a module function, as well as internal action id.

params.name: latency_limit_db
params.doc: Limit of latency in us (micro-seconds) for db operations. If a db operation executed via DB API v1 takes longer that its value, a message is printed in the logs, showing the first 50 characters of the db query.

params.name: latency_log
params.doc: Log level to print the messages related to latency.

params.name: listen
params.doc: Set the network addresses the SIP server should listen to. It can be an `IP address`, `hostname` or `network interface id` or combination of `protocol:address:port` (e.g., `udp:10.10.10.10:5060`). This parameter can be set multiple times in same configuration file, the server is listening on all addresses specified.

params.name: loadmodule
params.doc: Loads a module for later usage in the configuration script. The module is searched in the path specified by `loadpath` (or `mpath`).

params.name: loadmodulex
params.doc: Similar to `loadmodule` with the ability to evaluate variables in its parameter.

params.name: loadpath
params.doc: **Alias name:** `mpath`

params.name: local_rport
params.doc: Similar to **add_local_rport()** function, but done in a global scope, so the function does not have to be executed for each request.

params.name: log_engine_data
params.doc: Set specific data required by the log engine. See also the **log_engine_type**.

params.name: log_engine_type
params.doc: Specify what logging engine to be used and its initialization data. A logging engine is implemented as a module. Supported values are a matter of the module.

params.name: log_facility
params.doc: If Kamailio logs to syslog, you can control the facility for logging. Very useful when you want to divert all Kamailio logs to a different log file. See the man page syslog(3) for more details.

params.name: log_name
params.doc: Allows to configure a log_name prefix which will be used when printing to syslog -- it is also known as syslog tag, and the default value is the application name or full path that printed the log message. This is useful to filter log messages when running many instances of Kamailio on same server.

params.name: log_prefix
params.doc: Specify the text to be prefixed to the log messages printed by Kamailio while processing a SIP message (that is, when executing route blocks). It can contain script variables that are evaluated at runtime. See [#log_prefix_mode](#log_prefix_mode) about when/how evaluation is done.

params.name: log_prefix_mode
params.doc: Control if [log prefix](#log_prefix) is re-evaluated.

params.name: log_stderror
params.doc: With this parameter you can make Kamailio to write log and debug messages to standard error. Possible values are:

params.name: cfgengine
params.doc: Set the config interpreter engine for execution of the routing logic inside the configuration file. Default is the native interpreter.

params.name: maxbuffer
params.doc: The size in bytes multiplied by 2 not to be exceeded during the auto-probing procedure of discovering and increasing the maximum OS buffer size for receiving UDP messages (socket option SO_RCVBUF). Default value is 262144.

params.name: maxsndbuffer
params.doc: The size in bytes multiplied by 2 not to be exceeded during the auto-probing procedure of discovering and increasing the maximum OS buffer size for sending UDP messages (socket option SO_SNDBUF). Default value is 262144.

params.name: max_branches
params.doc: The maximum number of outgoing branches for each SIP request. It has impact on the size of destination set created in core (e.g., via append_branch()) as well as the serial and parallel forking done via tm module. It replaces the old defined constant MAX_BRANCHES.

params.name: max_recursive_level
params.doc: The parameters set the value of maximum recursive calls to blocks of actions, such as sub-routes or chained IF-ELSE (for the ELSE branches). Default is 256.

params.name: max_while_loops
params.doc: The parameters set the value of maximum loops that can be done within a "while". Comes as a protection to avoid infinite loops in config file execution. Default is 100. Setting to 0 disables the protection (you will still get a warning when you start Kamailio if you do something like while(1) {...}).

params.name: mcast
params.doc: This parameter can be used to set the interface that should join the multicast group. This is useful if you want to **listen** on a multicast address and don't want to depend on the kernel routing table for choosing an interface.

params.name: mcast_loopback
params.doc: It can be 'yes' or 'no'. If set to 'yes', multicast datagram are sent over loopback. Default value is 'no'.

params.name: mcast_ttl
params.doc: Set the value for multicast ttl. Default value is OS specific (usually 1).

params.name: memdbg
params.doc: **Alias name:** `mem_dbg`

params.name: memlog
params.doc: **Alias name:** `mem_log`

params.name: mem_add_size
params.doc: Size in bytes to be added for each chunk allocated by the internal `qm` (quick malloc) memory manager. It could be useful in cases when external libraries initialized to use `qm` expose issues of buffer overflow.

params.name: mem_join
params.doc: If set to 1, memory manager (e.g., q_malloc) does join of free fragments. It is effective if MEM_JOIN_FREE compile option is defined.

params.name: mem_safety
params.doc: If set to `1`, memory free operation does not call `abort()` for double freeing a pointer or freeing an invalid address. The server still prints the alerting log messages. If set to 0, the SIP server stops by calling `abort()` to generate a core file.

params.name: mem_status_mode
params.doc: If set to `1`, memory status dump for `qm` allocator will print details about used fragments. If set to `0`, the dump contains only free fragments. It can be set at runtime via cfg param framework (e.g., via `kamcmd`).

params.name: mem_summary
params.doc: Parameter to control printing of memory debugging information displayed on `exit` or `SIGUSR1`. The value can be composed by following flags:

params.name: mhomed
params.doc: Set the server to try to locate outbound interface on multihomed host. This parameter affects the selection of the outgoing socket for forwarding requests. By default is off (0) - it is rather time consuming. When deactivated, the incoming socket will be used or the first one for a different protocol, disregarding the destination location. When activated, Kamailio will select a socket that can reach the destination (to be able to connect to the remote address). (Kamailio opens a UDP socket to the destination, then it retrieves the local IP which was assigned by the operating system to the new UDP socket. Then this socket will be closed and the retrieved IP address will be used as IP address in the Via/Record-Route headers)

params.name: mlock_pages
params.doc: Locks all Kamailio pages into memory making it unswappable (in general one doesn't want his SIP proxy swapped out :-))

params.name: modinit_delay
params.doc: Number of microseconds to wait after initializing a module - useful to cope with systems where are rate limits on new connections to database or other systems.

params.name: modparam
params.doc: The modparam command will be used to set the options (parameters) for the loaded modules.

params.name: modparamx
params.doc: Similar to **modparam**, with ability to evaluate the variables in its parameters.

params.name: msg_recv_max_size
params.doc: Set the maximum size in bytes of a SIP message to be accepted by Kamailio.

params.name: msg_apply_changes_mode
params.doc: If set to `1`, the `msg_apply_changes()` is executed before the transaction for the SIP request is created. It can enable the use of `t_msg_apply_changes()` inside a `branch_route` block.

params.name: msg_clone_extra_size
params.doc: Size to be allocated extra when cloning the SIP request buffer to transaction. Useful when intending to do raw operations over the content of the buffer (e.g., SIP message body). The value is in bytes.

params.name: onsend_route_reply
params.doc: If set to 1 (yes, on), onsend_route block is executed for received replies that are sent out. Default is 0.

params.name: open_files_limit
params.doc: If set and bigger than the current open file limit, Kamailio will try to increase its open file limit to this number. Note: Kamailio must be started as root to be able to increase a limit past the hard limit (which, for open files, is `1024` on most systems). "Files" include network sockets, so you need one for every concurrent session (especially if you use connection-oriented transports, like TCP/TLS).

params.name: phone2tel
params.doc: By enabling this feature, Kamailio internally treats SIP URIs with user=phone parameter as TEL URIs. If you do not want this behavior, you have to turn it off.

params.name: pmtu_discovery
params.doc: If set to 1, the don't-fragment (DF) bit will be set in outbound IP packets, but no fragmentation from the kernel will be done for IPv4 and IPv6. This means that packets might be dropped and it is up to the user to reduce the packet size and try again.

params.name: port
params.doc: The port the SIP server listens to. The default value for it is 5060.

params.name: pv_buffer_size
params.doc: The size in bytes of internal buffer to print dynamic strings with pseudo-variables inside. The default value is 8192 (8kB). Please keep in mind that for xlog messages, there is a dedicated module parameter to set the internal buffer size.

params.name: pv_buffer_slots
params.doc: The number of internal buffer slots to print dynamic strings with pseudo-variables inside. The default value is 10.

params.name: pv_cache_limit
params.doc: The limit how many pv declarations in the cache after which an action is taken. Default value is 2048.

params.name: pv_cache_action
params.doc: Specify what action to be done when the size of pv cache is exceeded. If `0`, print a warning log message when the limit is exceeded. If `1`, warning log messages is printed and the cache systems tries to drop a `$sht(...)` declaration. Default is `0`.

params.name: rpc_exec_delta
params.doc: Specify the time interval (in seconds) required to wait before executing again an RPC command exported with the flag `RPC_EXEC_DELTA`. Practically it enables an execution rate limit for such command. The rate limiting is per RPC command.

params.name: rundir
params.doc: Alias: run_dir

params.name: received_route_mode
params.doc: Enable or disable the execution of `event_route[core:msg-received]` routing block or its corresponding Kemi callback.

params.name: reply_to_via
params.doc: If it is set to 1, any local reply is sent to the IP address advertised in top most Via of the request instead of the IP address from which the request was received. Default value is 0 (off).

params.name: route_locks_size
params.doc: Set the number of mutex locks to be used for synchronizing the execution of config script for messages sharing the same `Call-Id`. In other words, enables Kamailio to execute the config script sequentially for the requests and replies received within the same dialog -- a new message received within the same dialog waits until the previous one is routed out.

params.name: server_id
params.doc: A configurable unique server id that can be used to discriminate server instances within a cluster of servers when all other information, such as IP addresses are the same.

params.name: server_header
params.doc: Set the value of Server header for replies generated by Kamailio. It must contain the header name, but not the ending `CRLF`.

params.name: server_signature
params.doc: This parameter controls the "Server" header in any locally generated message.

params.name: shm_force_alloc
params.doc: Tries to pre-fault all the shared memory, before starting. When "on", start time will increase, but combined with mlock_pages will guarantee Kamailio will get all its memory from the beginning (no more kswapd slow downs)

params.name: shm_mem_size
params.doc: Set shared memory size (in Mb).

params.name: sip_parser_log
params.doc: Log level for printing debug messages for some of the SIP parsing errors.

params.name: sip_parser_mode
params.doc: Control sip parser behaviour.

params.name: sip_warning
params.doc: Can be `0` or `1`. If set to `1` (default value is `0`) a 'Warning' header is added to each reply generated by Kamailio. The header contains several details that help troubleshooting using the network traffic dumps, but might reveal details of your network infrastructure and internal SIP routing.

params.name: socket
params.doc: Specify an address to listen (bind) to, a simplified alternative to `listen` paramter that allows specifying the attributes using a structure style.

params.name: socket_workers
params.doc: Number of workers to process SIP traffic per listen socket - typical use is before a **listen** global parameter.

params.name: sql_buffer_size
params.doc: The size in bytes of the SQL buffer created for data base queries. For database drivers that use the core db_query library, this will be maximum size object that can be written or read from a database. Default value is 65535.

params.name: statistics
params.doc: Kamailio has built-in support for statistics counter. This means, these counters can be increased, decreased, read and cleared. The statistics counter are defined either by the core (e.g. tcp counters), by modules (e.g. 2xx_transactions by "tmx" module) or by the script writer using the "statistics" module.

params.name: stats_name_separator
params.doc: Specify the character used as a separator for the internal statistics' names. Default value is `_`.

params.name: tos
params.doc: The TOS (Type Of Service) to be used for the sent IP packages (both TCP and UDP).

params.name: udp_mtu
params.doc: Fallback to another protocol (`udp_mtu_try_proto` must be set also either globally or per packet) if the constructed request size is greater than udp_mtu.

params.name: udp_mtu_try_proto
params.doc: If `udp_mtu != 0` and udp forwarded request size (after adding all the "local" headers) `> udp_mtu`, use this protocol instead of udp. Only the Via header will be updated (e.g. The Record-Route will be the one built for udp).

params.name: udp_receiver_mode
params.doc: Specify how UDP traffic is received, either via a pool of processes per UDP socket or a single multi-threaded process with a thread per socket.

params.name: uri_host_extra_chars
params.doc: Specify additional chars that should be allowed in the host part of URI.

params.name: user
params.doc: **Alias name:** **uid**

params.name: user_agent_header
params.doc: Set the value of User-Agent header for requests generated by Kamailio. It must contain header name as well, but not the ending CRLF.

params.name: verbose_startup
params.doc: Control if printing routing tree and udp probing buffer debug messages should be printed at startup.

params.name: version_table
params.doc: Set the name of the table holding the table version. Useful if the proxy is sharing a database within a project and during upgrades. Default value is "version".

params.name: wait_worker1_mode
params.doc: Enable waiting for child SIP worker one to complete initialization, then create the other child worker processes.

params.name: wait_worker1_time
params.doc: How long to wait for child worker one to complete the initialization. In micro-seconds.

params.name: wait_worker1_usleep
params.doc: Waiting for child worker one to complete the initialization is done in a loop, which loop waits until wait_worker1_time passes. This parameter specifies how long after each iteration of that loop to wait in micro-seconds.

params.name: workdir
params.doc: **Alias name:** **wdir**

params.name: xavp_via_params
params.doc: Set the name of the XAVP of which subfields will be added as local `Via` -header parameters.

params.name: xavp_via_fields
params.doc: Set the name of xavp from where to take Via header field: address and port. Use them to build local Via header.

params.name: xavp_via_reply_params
params.doc: Set the name of the XAVP of which subfields will be added as header parameters to the top `Via` of the replies sent out.

params.name: dns
params.doc: This parameter controls if the SIP server will try doing a DNS lookup on the address in the Via header of a received sip request to decide if adding a `received=src_ip` parameter to the Via is necessary. Note that Vias containing DNS names (instead of IPs) should have `received=` added, so turning dns to yes is not recommended.

params.name: rev_dns
params.doc: **Alias name:** **dns_rev_via**

params.name: dns_cache_del_nonexp
params.doc: **Alias name:** **dns_cache_delete_nonexpired**

params.name: dns_cache_rec_pref
params.doc: dns cache record preference, determines how new DNS records are stored internally in relation to existing entries. Possible values: 0 - do not check duplicates 1 - prefer old records 2 - prefer new records 3 - prefer records with longer lifetime

params.name: dns_cache_flags
params.doc: dns cache specific resolver flags, used for overriding the default behaviour (low level). Possible values: 1 - ipv4 only: only DNS A requests are performed, even if Kamailio also listens on ipv6 addresses. 2 - ipv6 only: only DNS AAAA requests are performed. Ignored if dns_try_ipv6 is off or Kamailio doesn't listen on any ipv6 address. 4 - prefer ipv6: try first to resolve a host name to an ipv6 address (DNS AAAA request) and only if this fails try an ipv4 address (DNS A request). By default the ipv4 addresses are preferred.

params.name: dns_cache_gc_interval
params.doc: Interval in seconds after which the dns cache is garbage collected (default: 120 s)

params.name: dns_cache_init
params.doc: If off, the dns cache is not initialized at startup and cannot be enabled at runtime, this saves some memory.

params.name: dns_cache_mem
params.doc: Maximum memory used for the dns cache in KB (default 500 K)

params.name: dns_cache_negative_ttl
params.doc: Tells how long to keep negative DNS responses in cache. If set to 0, disables caching of negative responses. Default is 60 (seconds).

params.name: dns_naptr_ignore_rfc
params.doc: If the DNS lookup should ignore the remote side's protocol preferences, as indicated by the Order field in the NAPTR records and mandated by RFC 2915.

params.name: dns_retr_no
params.doc: Number of dns retransmissions before giving up. Default value is system specific, depends also on the '/etc/resolv.conf' content (usually 4).

params.name: dns_retr_time
params.doc: Time in seconds before retrying a dns request. Default value is system specific, depends also on the '/etc/resolv.conf' content (usually 5s).

params.name: dns_search_full_match
params.doc: When name was resolved using dns search list, check the domain added in the answer matches with one from the search list (small performance hit, but more safe)

params.name: dns_servers_no
params.doc: How many dns servers from the ones defined in '/etc/resolv.conf' will be used. Default value is to use all of them.

params.name: dns_srv_lb
params.doc: **Alias name:** **dns_srv_loadbalancing**

params.name: dns_try_ipv6
params.doc: Can be 'yes' or 'no'. If it is set to 'yes' and a DNS lookup fails, it will retry it for ipv6 (AAAA record). Default value is 'no'.

params.name: dns_try_naptr
params.doc: Enable NAPTR support according to RFC 3263 (see doc/tutorials/dns.txt for more info)

params.name: dns_sctp_pref,
params.doc: **Alias name:** **dns_sctp_preference, dns_tcp_preference, dns_tls_preference, dns_udp_preference**

params.name: dns_use_search_list
params.doc: Can be 'yes' or 'no'. If set to 'no', the search list in '/etc/resolv.conf' will be ignored (=> fewer lookups => gives up faster). Default value is 'yes'.

params.name: use_dns_cache
params.doc: **Alias name:** **dns_use_cache**

params.name: use_dns_failover
params.doc: **Alias name:** **dns_use_failover**

params.name: disable_tcp
params.doc: Global parameter to disable TCP support in the SIP server. Default value is `no`.

params.name: tcp_accept_aliases
params.doc: If a message received over a tcp connection has "alias" in its via a new tcp alias port will be created for the connection the message came from (the alias port will be set to the via one).

params.name: tcp_accept_haproxy
params.doc: Enable the internal TCP stack to expect a PROXY-protocol-formatted header as the first message of the connection. Both the human-readable (v1) and binary-encoded (v2) variants of the protocol are supported. This option is typically useful if you are behind a TCP load-balancer, such as HAProxy or an AWS' ELB, and allows the load-balancer to provide connection information regarding the upstream client. This enables the use of IP-based ACLs, even behind a load-balancer.

params.name: tcp_accept_hep3
params.doc: Enable internal TCP receiving stack to accept HEP3 packets. This option has to be set to **yes** on a Kamailio instance acting as Homer SIPCapture server that is supposed to receive HEP3 packets over TCP/TLS.

params.name: tcp_accept_iplimit
params.doc: Set limit for accepted connections from the same IP address.

params.name: tcp_accept_no_cl
params.doc: Control whether to throw or not error when there is no Content-Length header for requests received over TCP. It is required to be set to **yes** for XCAP traffic sent over HTTP/1.1 which does not use Content-Length header, but splits large bodies in many chunks. The module **sanity** can be used then to restrict this permission to HTTP traffic only, testing in route block in order to stay RFC3261 compliant about this mandatory header for SIP requests over TCP.

params.name: tcp_accept_unique
params.doc: If set to `1`, reject duplicate connections coming from same source IP and port.

params.name: tcp_async
params.doc: **Alias name:** **tcp_buf_write**

params.name: tcp_check_timer
params.doc: Set the check interval (in seconds) for tcp connections. It is used to check if there was any data received on new connections or if the receiving of SIP messages takes too long. See also `tcp_msg_data_timeout` and `tcp_msg_read_timeout`.

params.name: tcp_children
params.doc: Number of children processes to be created for reading from TCP connections. If no value is explicitly set, the same number of TCP children as UDP children (see "children" parameter) will be used.

params.name: tcp_clone_rcvbuf
params.doc: Control if the received buffer should be cloned from the TCP stream, needed by functions working inside the SIP message buffer (such as msg_apply_changes()).

params.name: tcp_connection_lifetime
params.doc: Lifetime in seconds for TCP sessions. TCP sessions which are inactive for longer than **tcp_connection_lifetime** will be closed by Kamailio. Default value is defined is `120`. Setting this value to 0 will close the TCP connection pretty quick.

params.name: tcp_connection_match
params.doc: If set to `1`, try to be more strict in matching outbound TCP connections, attempting to lookup first the connection using also local port, not only the local IP and remote IP+port.

params.name: tcp_connect_timeout
params.doc: Time in seconds before an ongoing attempt to establish a new TCP connection will be aborted. Lower this value for faster detection of TCP connection problems. The default value is 10s.

params.name: tcp_conn_wq_max
params.doc: Maximum bytes queued for write allowed per connection. Attempting to queue more bytes would result in an error and in the connection being closed (too slow). If tcp_buf_write is not enabled, it has no effect.

params.name: tcp_crlf_ping
params.doc: Enable SIP outbound TCP keep-alive using PING-PONG (CRLFCRLF - CRLF).

params.name: tcp_defer_accept
params.doc: Tcp accepts will be delayed until some data is received (improves performance on proxies with lots of opened tcp connections). See linux `tcp(7)` `TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT` or freebsd `ACCF_DATA(0)`. For now linux and freebsd only.

params.name: tcp_delayed_ack
params.doc: Initial ACK for opened connections will be delayed and sent with the first data segment (see linux tcp(7) TCP_QUICKACK). For now linux only.

params.name: tcp_fd_cache
params.doc: If enabled FDs used for sending will be cached inside the process calling tcp_send (performance increase for sending over tcp at the cost of slightly slower connection closing and extra FDs kept open)

params.name: tcp_keepalive
params.doc: Enables keepalive for tcp (sets SO_KEEPALIVE socket option)

params.name: tcp_keepcnt
params.doc: Number of keepalives sent before dropping the connection (TCP_KEEPCNT socket option). Linux only.

params.name: tcp_keepidle
params.doc: Time before starting to send keepalives, if the connection is idle (TCP_KEEPIDLE socket option). Linux only.

params.name: tcp_keepintvl
params.doc: Time interval between keepalive probes, when the previous probe failed (TCP_KEEPINTVL socket option). Linux only.

params.name: tcp_linger2
params.doc: Lifetime of orphaned sockets in FIN_WAIT2 state (overrides tcp_fin_timeout on, see linux tcp(7) TCP_LINGER2). Linux only.

params.name: tcp_listen_backlog
params.doc: The value for listen backlog parameter for TCP/TLS sockets.

params.name: tcp_main_threads
params.doc: If set to 1, the TLS read and encode (for sending) operations are done by threads created by the main TCP process. If set to 0, the operations are done in the old-style, mostly by the SIP worker processes.

params.name: tcp_max_connections
params.doc: Maximum number of tcp connections (if the number is exceeded no new tcp connections will be accepted). Default is defined in tcp_init.h: #define DEFAULT_TCP_MAX_CONNECTIONS 2048

params.name: tcp_msg_data_timeout
params.doc: Duration in seconds for how long to wait till data is received on a new tcp connection. Default 20.

params.name: tcp_msg_read_timeout
params.doc: Duration in seconds for how long to wait till a SIP message is read on a new tcp connection. Default 20.

params.name: tcp_no_connect
params.doc: Stop outgoing TCP connects (also stops TLS) by setting tcp_no_connect to yes.

params.name: tcp_poll_method
params.doc: Poll method used (by default the best one for the current OS is selected). For available types see io_wait.c and poll_types.h: none, poll, epoll_lt, epoll_et, sigio_rt, select, kqueue, /dev/poll

params.name: tcp_rd_buf_size
params.doc: Buffer size used for tcp reads. A high buffer size increases performance on server with few connections and lot of traffic on them, but also increases memory consumption (so for lots of connection is better to use a low value). Note also that this value limits the maximum message size (SIP, HTTP) that can be received over tcp.

params.name: tcp_reuse_port
params.doc: Allows reuse of TCP ports. This means, for example, that the same TCP ports on which Kamailio is listening on, can be used as source ports of new TCP connections when acting as an UAC. Kamailio must have been compiled in a system implementing SO_REUSEPORT (Linux \> 3.9.0, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, MacOSX). This parameter takes effect only if also the system on which Kamailio is running on supports SO_REUSEPORT.

params.name: tcp_script_mode
params.doc: Specify if connection should be closed (set to CONN_ERROR) if processing the received message results in error (that can also be due to negative return code from a configuration script main route block). If set to 1, the processing continues with the connection open.

params.name: tcp_send_timeout
params.doc: Time in seconds after a TCP connection will be closed if it is not available for writing in this interval (and Kamailio wants to send something on it). Lower this value for faster detection of broken TCP connections. The default value is 10s.

params.name: tcp_source_ipv4,
params.doc: Set the source IP for all outbound TCP connections. If setting of the IP fails, the TCP connection will use the default IP address.

params.name: tcp_syncnt
params.doc: Number of SYN retransmissions before aborting a connect attempt (see linux tcp(7) TCP_SYNCNT). Linux only.

params.name: tcp_wait_data
params.doc: Specify how long to wait (in milliseconds) to wait for data on tcp connections in certain cases. Now applies when reading on tcp connection for haproxy protocol.

params.name: tcp_wq_blk_size
params.doc: Block size used for tcp async writes. It should be big enough to hold a few datagrams. If it's smaller than a datagram (in fact a tcp write()) size, it will be rounded up. It has no influenced on the number of datagrams queued (for that see tcp_conn_wq_max or tcp_wq_max). It has mostly debugging and testing value (can be ignored).

params.name: tcp_wq_max
params.doc: Maximum bytes queued for write allowed globally. It has no effect if tcp_buf_write is not enabled.

params.name: tls_port_no
params.doc: The port the SIP server listens to for TLS connections.

params.name: tls_max_connections
params.doc: Maximum number of TLS connections (if the number is exceeded no new TLS connections will be accepted). It cannot exceed tcp_max_connections.

params.name: tls_threads_mode
params.doc: Control how to initialize the internal multi-threading system that impacts libssl 3.x.

params.name: disable_sctp
params.doc: Global parameter to disable SCTP support in the SIP server. See also `enable_sctp`.

params.name: sctp_children
params.doc: sctp children no (similar to udp children)

params.name: sctp_socket_rcvbuf
params.doc: Size for the sctp socket receive buffer

params.name: sctp_socket_sndbuf
params.doc: Size for the sctp socket send buffer

params.name: sctp_autoclose
params.doc: Number of seconds before autoclosing an idle association (default: `180` s). Can be changed at runtime, but it will affect only new associations. E.g.:

params.name: sctp_send_ttl
params.doc: Number of milliseconds before an unsent message/chunk is dropped (default: `32000` ms or `32` s). Can be changed at runtime, e.g.:

params.name: sctp_send_retries
params.doc: How many times to attempt re-sending a message on a re-opened association, if the sctp stack did give up sending it (it's not related to sctp protocol level retransmission). Useful to improve reliability with peers that reboot/restart or fail over to another machine.

params.name: sctp_assoc_tracking
params.doc: Controls whether or not sctp associations are tracked inside Kamailio. Turning it off would result in less memory being used and slightly better performance, but it will also disable some other features that depend on it (e.g. `sctp_assoc_reuse`). Default: yes.

params.name: sctp_assoc_reuse
params.doc: Controls sctp association reuse. For now only association reuse for replies is affected by it. Default: `yes`. Depends on `sctp_assoc_tracking` being on.

params.name: sctp_max_assocs
params.doc: Maximum number of allowed open sctp associations. -1 means maximum allowed by the OS. Default: -1. Can be changed at runtime (e.g.: `kamcmd cfg.seti sctp max_assocs 10`). When the maximum associations number is exceeded and a new associations is opened by a remote host, the association will be immediately closed. However it is possible that some SIP packets get through (especially if they are sent early, as part of the 4-way handshake).

params.name: sctp_srto_initial
params.doc: Initial value of the retr. timeout, used in RTO calculations (default: OS specific).

params.name: sctp_srto_max
params.doc: Maximum value of the retransmission timeout (RTO) (default: OS specific).

params.name: sctp_srto_min
params.doc: Minimum value of the retransmission timeout (RTO) (default: OS specific).

params.name: sctp_asocmaxrxt
params.doc: Maximum retransmissions attempts per association (default: OS specific). It should be set to `sctp_pathmaxrxt` `*` no. of expected paths.

params.name: sctp_init_max_attempts
params.doc: Maximum INIT retransmission attempts (default: OS specific).

params.name: sctp_init_max_timeo
params.doc: Maximum INIT retransmission timeout (RTO max for INIT). Default: OS specific.

params.name: sctp_hbinterval
params.doc: sctp heartbeat interval. Setting it to -1 will disable the heartbeats. Default: OS specific.

params.name: sctp_pathmaxrxt
params.doc: Maximum retransmission attempts per path (see also sctp_asocmaxrxt). Default: OS specific.

params.name: sctp_sack_delay
params.doc: Delay until an ACK is generated after receiving a packet. Default: OS specific.

params.name: sctp_sack_freq
params.doc: Number of packets received before an ACK is sent (without waiting for the `sack_delay` to expire). Default: OS specific.

params.name: sctp_max_burst
params.doc: Maximum burst of packets that can be emitted by an association. Default: OS specific.

params.name: udp4_raw
params.doc: Enables raw socket support for sending UDP IPv4 datagrams (40-50% performance increase on linux multi-cpu).

params.name: udp4_raw_mtu
params.doc: MTU value used for UDP IPv4 packets when udp4_raw is enabled. It should be set to the minimum MTU of all the network interfaces that could be used for sending. The default value is 1500. Note that on BSDs it does not need to be set (if set it will be ignored, the proper MTU will be used automatically by the kernel). On Linux it should be set.

params.name: udp4_raw_ttl
params.doc: TTL value used for UDP IPv4 packets when udp4_raw is enabled. By default it is set to auto mode (`-1`), meaning that the same TTL will be used as for normal UDP sockets.

params.name: dst_blocklist_expire
params.doc: **Alias name:** **dst_blocklist_ttl**

params.name: dst_blocklist_gc_interval
params.doc: How often the garbage collection will run (eliminating old, expired entries).

params.name: dst_blocklist_init
params.doc: If off, the blocklist is not initialized at startup and cannot be enabled at runtime, this saves some memory.

params.name: dst_blocklist_mem
params.doc: Maximum shared memory amount used for keeping the blocklisted destinations.

params.name: use_dst_blocklist
params.doc: Enable the destination blocklist: Each failed send attempt will cause the destination to be added to the blocklist. Before any send, this blocklist will be checked and if a match is found, the send is no longer attempted (an error is returned immediately).

params.name: real_time
params.doc: Sets real time priority for all the Kamailio processes, or the timers (bitmask).

params.name: rt_policy
params.doc: Real time scheduling policy, `0 = SCHED_OTHER`, `1= SCHED_RR` and `2=SCHED_FIFO`

params.name: rt_prio
params.doc: Real time priority used for everything except the timers, if `real_time` is enabled.

params.name: rt_timer1_policy
params.doc: **Alias name:** **rt_ftimer_policy**

params.name: rt_timer1_prio
params.doc: **Alias name:** **rt_fast_timer_prio, rt_ftimer_prio**

params.name: rt_timer2_policy
params.doc: **Alias name:** **rt_stimer_policy**

params.name: rt_timer2_prio
params.doc: **Alias name:** **rt_stimer_prio**

pvars.name: $cT

pvars.name: $defv

pvars.name: $dip

pvars.name: $fn

pvars.name: $mi

pvars.name: $ml

pvars.name: $mt

pvars.name: $pn
